facts.t: The GST Council's recommendations are not binding
facts.d: In Mohit Minerals (2022) the Supreme Court held that Article 279A recommendations are persuasive only, since both Parliament and state legislatures hold simultaneous power under Article 246A. The Council's authority rests on political consensus, not legal compulsion.

facts.t: States can switch the CBI off at the border
facts.d: The Delhi Special Police Establishment Act requires state consent for the CBI to operate. Several states have withdrawn that general consent, so the agency must seek case-by-case permission or a court order to investigate there.

Article 239AA gives the National Capital Territory a legislature and a Council of Ministers while keeping police, public order and land with the Union. That single asymmetric arrangement has generated more Supreme Court litigation than most full states.

bank.q: In Mohit Minerals the Supreme Court held that GST Council recommendations are:
o: Binding on both Parliament and state legislatures
Binding only where two-thirds of states concur
bank.e: Persuasive, not binding — because Article 246A confers simultaneous legislative power on both the Union and the states.

bank.q: Consider the following as combative instances in Centre–State relations:
s: States withdrawing general consent to the Central Bureau of Investigation.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are combative. One Nation One Ration Card is a standard example of cooperative welfare delivery.

bank.q: Match List I (policy area) with List II (its competitive expression):
pairs: 3. SEQI and the Performance Grading Index
4. Health, SDG, Water and Innovation indices
bank.e: NITI's indices, investment summits for ease of doing business, renewables and EV policy for environment, and school-education indices for education.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a cooperative federalism example?
o: NDMA and SDMA coordination on disaster management
bank.e: The farm laws are the standard combative example — a conflict over legislative competence and the absence of consultation, ending in repeal.

bank.as: The Aspirational Districts Programme attracts criticism despite being a cooperative initiative.
bank.rs: Its central indicators are said to ignore local priorities.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The same programme is simultaneously cooperative in design, competitive through delta rankings, and contested on indicator choice.

bank.q: With reference to Article 239AA, consider the following statements:
s: It gives the National Capital Territory a legislature and a Council of Ministers.
Police, public order and land remain with the Union.
It has generated repeated disputes involving the Lieutenant Governor.
bank.e: All three are correct — the asymmetric design is precisely what makes Delhi a recurring federal flashpoint.

bank.q: All of the following are combative instances in the environment and disaster domain EXCEPT:
bank.e: CAMPA is listed as cooperative — compensatory afforestation funds routed to states for forest restoration.

bank.q: Boycotts of NITI Aayog Governing Council meetings are cited as an instance of:
bank.e: Combative — the stated grievance is fiscal centralisation, so states withdraw from the very platform designed for cooperation.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about centrally sponsored schemes:
s: Jal Jeevan Mission and PMAY operate on cost-sharing between Centre and states.
States compete on speed and coverage of implementation.
States have objected to fund-sharing ratios and branding conditions.
bank.e: All three are correct — the same scheme family sits in all three columns of the matrix at once.

bank.q: Anti-Hindi-imposition movements belong to which cell of the federalism matrix?
o: Cooperative, in the language and culture area
Competitive, in the language and culture area
Combative, in the language and culture area
bank.e: Combative. The cooperative expression in that area is the Eighth Schedule and classical-language recognition; the competitive one is tourism, heritage and GI tags.
